text:
jordan: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a different approach for eviction coordination: a "sticky watermark" that travels with a prefix lease so we avoid oscillating fetches when prefixes bounce between shards.

samira: quick sketch — what do you mean by "sticky watermark"?

jordan: imagine each prefix has a logical eviction_watermark (EW). When a shard demotes a prefix (evicts), it stamps the prefix with a watermark (logical epoch + seq). Future owners must advance past that EW before they fully evict again. basically a short-lived memory of recent eviction decisions.

devon: so it's like a lease-adjacent marker that prevents churn when ownership flips?

jordan: exactly. avoids a hot prefix being repeatedly fetched/evicted on handoff loops. also lets prefetch/backpressure know not to aggressively rehydrate a recently-evicted prefix.

anya: what's the lifecycle? how long does EW live? per-tenant config?

jordan: EW = {epoch, counter, ttl_ms}. owner sets EW on demote. propagated in handoff meta. TTL is short (e.g., 30s) but bumped on repeated demotes. config per-pool.

samira: are we relying on clocks? sounds like we'd need monotonic counters per-shard.
jordan: no wall-clock; use local counter + epoch from sequencer/lease id. monotonic compare: (epoch, counter) lexicographic.

devon: curious about correctness: could EW create staleness where a legitimate demote is blocked because old owner left EW too high?
jordan: tradeoff. We only block aggressive immediate re-eviction. fallback: after TTL expires, new owner can demote normally. also allow forced-demote by operator or low-memory path (hard-evict) that increments counter to a new epoch.

anya: any changes to client read path? read-after-write semantics?
jordan: read path unchanged. This is an ownership/eviction coordination primitive, not a cache-consistency protocol. We keep existing prefix pinning for in-flight requests. EW only affects decision to preemptively evict/deny prefetch.

devon: sounds useful. need to think about multi-tenant fairness: could a noisy tenant keep bumping EW to hog memory?
jordan: we already have tenant credits + eviction priority. EW interacts with credits: if tenant exhausted credits, EW is ignored (i.e., hard eviction allowed). so fairness preserved.

samira: how do we propagate EW during handoff? include in the handoff payload metadata?
jordan: yep. handoff message includes last_eviction_watermark. receiver merges: receiver.EW = max(receiver.EW, incoming.EW). also persist to local ephemeral store (not durable).

devon: how to implement compare/merge deterministically? show tiny pseudocode pls.

jordan: sure:

```
struct EW { u64 epoch; u64 counter; u64 expires_at_ms; }
function max_ew(a, b):
  if a.epoch > b.epoch return a
  if b.epoch > a.epoch return b
  return (a.counter >= b.counter) ? a : b
function merge_ew(a, b):
  m = max_ew(a, b)
  m.expires_at_ms = max(a.expires_at_ms, b.expires_at_ms)
  return m
```

jordan: receiver will start honoring merged EW for prefetch/admit decisions.

anya: metrics we need: EW_set_count, EW_bumped_count, EW_blocked_prefetch_count, EW_forced_hard_evictions. also track average EW_ttl extension per-prefix.

samira: what about cross-region handoffs where network delays are high? TTL might expire mid-flight.
jordan: fine-grained: include original_set_ts (logical). if receiver sees incoming EW already expired, drop. also handoff ack includes whether receiver honored EW; origin can bump before final handoff completes.

devon: how will this interact with our existing demote/backpressure signals?
jordan: demote sets EW; backpressure checks EW before allocating prefetch credits; admission returns DENY_EW if EW is active. we add a small code path:

```
if tenant.credits == 0: allow_hard_evict()
elif prefix.EW.active(): deny_prefetch("EW")
else allow_prefetch()
```

devon: tests? we should run riot scenarios: rapid handoff loops, cross-shard ping-pong, and TTL exhaustion races.

jordan: yep. test matrix: single-hotkey ping-pong; many-tenant stress with credits; CI smoke that forces hard-evict path. I'll add fuzz harness for EW merges.

anya: ops concerns: need a lightweight trace/span when EW blocks something so SRE can see these as "EW-blocked-prefetch" events.
jordan: will add tracing tag ev.watermark={epoch,counter}. also a warn-level log when EW causes >5% of prefetches to be denied for a tenant.

samira: do we need a migration? existing nodes should treat missing EW as null; backward compat ok?
jordan: yes, compat is simple: missing metadata = EW(0,0,0). New nodes will set/propagate EW but old ones ignore; during rollout we'll see reduced efficacy until fully rolled out.

devon: any potential for EW to be replayed maliciously by compromised shards? security note: handshake must be authenticated in the control plane.
jordan: agreed — handoff meta is already signed by node TLS identity. no new surface.

anya: overall LGTM from me. can you open an RFC PR with design + tests + metrics?
jordan: will do. PR will include simulation results showing 40-60% reduction in rehydration churn on ping-pong scenarios.

samira: nice. thanks jordan — this looks like a practical middle ground between doing nothing and a heavyweight distributed lease. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-checklist — remember to add feature-flag `eviction.sticky_watermark=true` and opsdoc entry.

jordan: adding feature flag and rollout plan to the PR.

devon: one more question: TTL tuning — is 30s safe? maybe 15s on high-memory pools?
jordan: default 30s but pool-configurable. will add adaptive heuristic: if handoff_rate(prefix) > X, bump TTL up to 2x, capped.

anya: cool. thanks — eager to see the PR.

jordan: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/482 (draft) — will link tests in thread when ready.

samira: awesome. follow-up: add a short runbook step in evictions doc for "EW-stall" troubleshooting.

jordan: done in PR checklist.

devon: marking this thread resolved for now.

jordan: thanks all! :party:
